title: Lipid Cut-Points: Triglyceride Bands, LDL-C 190, Statin Intensity, Metabolic Syndrome and Children
summary: Learn the decision numbers around a lipid panel: how triglyceride categories differ between guidelines, why LDL-C ≥190 mg/dL triggers a high-intensity statin without a risk calculation, how statin intensity is defined, the five metabolic syndrome criteria and the NHLBI cut-points for children.

reviewer.note: Teaches Ch. 18 Hits 3, 5, 7, 8 and 15 and the triglyceride, LDL-C, children, HDL, metabolic syndrome, statin-initiation and statin-intensity rows of the Number Vault. Checked against the 2018 AHA/ACC multisociety guideline (Grundy 2019, PMC page read via a page-fetch tool), the NHLBI 2011 pediatric expert panel (read via a page-fetch tool), Hernandez 2021, Kassi 2011 and Nordestgaard 2016. Hit 3’s four triglyceride bands (<150 / 150–199 / 200–499 / ≥500) do not match any of the three current schemes tabulated by Hernandez 2021 (register flag rv-tg-categories-scheme). Hit 8’s triglyceride ≥150 matches the consensus definition, but the 2018 AHA/ACC risk-enhancer table tallies triglycerides >175, and waist cut-offs are ethnicity-specific (register flag rv-mets-cutoffs-guideline). Not taught: the FH-suspect threshold of LDL ≥160 under age 20 (Hit 5; pending), the Friedewald, Lp(a), Tangier, posture, EDTA and timing rows of the Number Vault (other lessons or pending).

objectives: Compare triglyceride classifications of the 2018 AHA/ACC, Endocrine Society and ESC guidelines and state why severe hypertriglyceridaemia is treated.
Apply the LDL-C ≥190 mg/dL rule and define high-, moderate- and low-intensity statin therapy.
Count metabolic syndrome criteria and classify a child’s total and LDL cholesterol with NHLBI 2011 cut-points.

scenes.title: Three lipid reports
scenes.altText: Invented scenario: three lipid reports reach the same desk — (1) a 38-year-old with no heart disease, LDL-C 210 mg/dL; (2) a 50-year-old with triglycerides 620 mg/dL; (3) a 14-year-old with LDL-C 135 mg/dL. Question token: “Which number triggers what?”

cues.text: An invented morning: three lipid reports. A thirty-eight-year-old with no heart disease and an LDL cholesterol of two hundred and ten.
A fifty-year-old with triglycerides of six hundred and twenty. And a fourteen-year-old with an LDL cholesterol of one hundred and thirty-five.
Each number crosses a different line. Which number triggers what?

scenes.title: Triglyceride cut-points depend on the guideline
scenes.altText: Three schematic scales of fasting triglyceride classification (mg/dL), from the comparison table in Hernandez 2021. 2018 AHA/ACC multisociety: normal <175, moderate 175–499, severe ≥500. Endocrine Society: normal <150, mild 150–199, moderate 200–999, severe 1000–1999, very severe ≥2000. European Society of Cardiology: normal <150, mild-moderate 150–880, severe >880. Treatment card (Hernandez 2021 review): for severe hypertriglyceridaemia, fibrates and/or high-dose prescription omega-3 fatty acids are first-line drugs, aiming to bring triglycerides below 500 mg/dL and reduce the risk of acute pancreatitis; fibrates lower triglycerides by about 25–50%.

cues.text: Triglyceride categories are not universal. The 2018 American multisociety guideline calls under one hundred and seventy-five normal, one seventy-five to four ninety-nine moderate, and five hundred or more severe.
The Endocrine Society calls under one fifty normal and one fifty to one ninety-nine mild. Its moderate band runs to nine ninety-nine, and severe starts at one thousand.
The European Society of Cardiology also starts at one fifty, but calls everything up to eight hundred and eighty mild to moderate.
For severe hypertriglyceridaemia, a 2021 review names fibrates or high-dose omega-3 fatty acids as first-line drugs, aiming for triglycerides below five hundred to lower pancreatitis risk.

scenes.title: LDL-C 190 and statin intensity
scenes.altText: Decision card (2018 AHA/ACC guideline): severe primary hypercholesterolaemia, LDL-C ≥190 mg/dL — begin high-intensity statin therapy without calculating 10-year ASCVD risk; if LDL-C stays ≥100 mg/dL, adding ezetimibe is reasonable. The EAS/EFLM consensus flags adult LDL-C >190 mg/dL as suspicious for heterozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia. Intensity table (guideline Table 3): high intensity lowers LDL-C by ≥50% (atorvastatin 40–80 mg, rosuvastatin 20–40 mg); moderate 30–49% (for example atorvastatin 10–20 mg, rosuvastatin 5–10 mg, simvastatin 20–40 mg); low <30% (for example simvastatin 10 mg, pravastatin 10–20 mg). Primary-prevention card: adults 40–75 years without diabetes, LDL-C 70–189 mg/dL and 10-year ASCVD risk ≥7.5% — start a moderate-intensity statin if the risk discussion favours it.

cues.text: Now LDL cholesterol. At one hundred and ninety or more, the 2018 guideline calls it severe primary hypercholesterolaemia: start a high-intensity statin without calculating ten-year risk at all.
If LDL stays at one hundred or more on the statin, adding ezetimibe is reasonable. A European consensus also flags adult LDL above one ninety as suspicious for familial hypercholesterolaemia.

Statin intensity is defined by the expected LDL drop. High intensity lowers LDL by fifty percent or more: atorvastatin forty to eighty, or rosuvastatin twenty to forty milligrams. Moderate lowers it thirty to forty-nine percent; low, under thirty.

In primary prevention below one ninety, a risk calculation guides the decision. Adults forty to seventy-five without diabetes, with LDL seventy to one eighty-nine and a ten-year risk of seven point five percent or more, start a moderate-intensity statin if the discussion favours it.

scenes.title: Metabolic syndrome and children’s cut-points
scenes.altText: Metabolic syndrome card (consensus definition incorporating IDF and AHA/NHLBI, as summarised by Kassi 2011): any 3 of — elevated waist circumference (population- and country-specific; AHA/NHLBI uses ≥102 cm men, ≥88 cm women; IDF uses ≥94/80 cm for Europids and ≥90/80 cm for South and South-East Asian, Chinese and Japanese people), triglycerides ≥150 mg/dL, HDL-C <40 mg/dL men / <50 mg/dL women, BP ≥130/85 mmHg, fasting glucose ≥100 mg/dL. Note: the 2018 AHA/ACC risk-enhancer table tallies triglycerides >175 mg/dL instead. Children card (NHLBI 2011 Expert Panel): total cholesterol acceptable <170, borderline-high 170–199, high ≥200; LDL-C acceptable <110, borderline-high 110–129, high ≥130 mg/dL. Hook answers: (1) LDL-C 210 → high-intensity statin, no risk calculation; (2) TG 620 → severe in the 2018 AHA/ACC scheme (moderate in the Endocrine Society scheme, mild-moderate in the ESC scheme); (3) LDL-C 135 at age 14 → high (≥130).

cues.text: Metabolic syndrome is any three of five: a large waist, triglycerides of one fifty or more, low HDL under forty in men or fifty in women, blood pressure of one thirty over eighty-five or more, and fasting glucose of one hundred or more.

The waist cut-off depends on the population. The American definition uses one hundred and two and eighty-eight centimetres; the IDF uses ninety and eighty for South Asian, Chinese and Japanese people.
Children have their own table. Total cholesterol under one seventy is acceptable and two hundred or more is high. LDL under one ten is acceptable and one thirty or more is high.
Back to the hook. LDL two ten: high-intensity statin, no calculator. Triglycerides six twenty: severe in the 2018 American scheme. The teenager’s LDL of one thirty-five: high.

scenes.title: Three classic traps
scenes.altText: Three trap cards: “Triglycerides 150–199 are borderline high in every guideline” (✓ categories depend on the guideline; the 2018 AHA/ACC scheme calls <175 normal); “LDL-C 195 mg/dL: calculate 10-year risk first” (✓ at ≥190 start a high-intensity statin without a risk calculation); “Use adult cut-offs for a 12-year-old” (✓ children: LDL-C ≥130 and total cholesterol ≥200 mg/dL are high).

cues.text: Trap one: triglycerides of one fifty to one ninety-nine are borderline high everywhere. No: the categories depend on the guideline, and the 2018 American scheme calls under one seventy-five normal.
Trap two: an LDL of one ninety-five needs a ten-year risk calculation first. No: at one ninety or more, start a high-intensity statin without one.
Trap three: judge a twelve-year-old by adult cut-offs. No: in children an LDL of one thirty or a total cholesterol of two hundred is already high.

props.title: ✗ “Adult cut-offs fit a child.”
lines: ✓ Child: LDL ≥ 130 or TC ≥ 200 is high

scenes.title: 190 skips the calculator
scenes.altText: Memory aid: “190 SKIPS the calculator; 500 GUARDS the pancreas; 3 of 5 MAKES the syndrome; HALF the LDL gone = HIGH intensity. Kids are fine under 170 and 110, high at 200 and 130.” Tokens: 190 = no calculator · 500 = pancreas · 3 of 5 = syndrome · ≥50% = high intensity. A card lists where the aid breaks.

cues.text: Memory aid: one ninety skips the calculator. Five hundred guards the pancreas. Three of five makes the syndrome. Half the LDL gone means high intensity. And children are fine under one seventy and one ten, high at two hundred and one thirty.

Where it breaks: triglyceride bands and the metabolic syndrome triglyceride cut-off differ between guidelines; waist cut-offs depend on ethnicity; these are United States and European rules, and Philippine guidelines are not covered here.

scenes.title: Takeaway
scenes.altText: Two tokens: “LDL-C ≥190 → high-intensity statin (≥50% LDL drop), no risk calculation · severe TG ≥500 (US 2018) → treat to prevent pancreatitis”, “Metabolic syndrome = any 3 of 5 · children: TC ≥200, LDL-C ≥130 mg/dL high”.

cues.text: An LDL cholesterol of 190 mg/dL or more calls for a high-intensity statin without a risk calculation, severe hypertriglyceridemia starts at 500 mg/dL in the 2018 American guideline, metabolic syndrome needs three of five criteria, and children are already high at a total cholesterol of 200 or an LDL cholesterol of 130 mg/dL.

props.label: LDL ≥ 190 → high-intensity statin, no calculator · TG ≥ 500 → pancreas
Metabolic syndrome: any 3 of 5 · child TC ≥ 200, LDL ≥ 130 high

explanation.what: Plain language: a lipid report is read against decision numbers. Very high triglycerides risk pancreatitis; very high LDL cholesterol gets strong cholesterol-lowering medicine straight away; a cluster of risk factors defines metabolic syndrome; and children are judged by their own, lower table. Scientific terms: hypertriglyceridaemia (moderate, severe), severe primary hypercholesterolaemia, familial hypercholesterolaemia (FH), statin intensity, 10-year ASCVD risk (Pooled Cohort Equations), risk-enhancing factors, metabolic syndrome, NHLBI pediatric cut-points (acceptable, borderline-high, high).
explanation.why: The 2018 AHA/ACC guideline exempts LDL-C ≥190 mg/dL from 10-year risk assessment, so treatment starts without a calculator. Severe hypertriglyceridaemia is treated primarily to reduce acute pancreatitis risk. Statin intensity is defined by the average percentage LDL-C fall, which varies between individuals. Pediatric cut-points are based on population percentiles (about the 75th for borderline-high and 95th for high).
explanation.measure: Triglycerides (mg/dL): 2018 AHA/ACC normal <175, moderate 175–499, severe ≥500; Endocrine Society normal <150, mild 150–199, moderate 200–999, severe ≥1000; ESC normal <150, mild-moderate 150–880, severe >880. LDL-C ≥190: high-intensity statin, no risk calculation; ezetimibe reasonable if still ≥100. Intensity: high ≥50% (atorvastatin 40–80, rosuvastatin 20–40 mg), moderate 30–49%, low <30%. Adults 40–75, LDL-C 70–189, 10-year risk ≥7.5%: moderate-intensity statin if discussion favours. Metabolic syndrome: any 3 of waist (population-specific), TG ≥150, HDL <40 M/<50 W, BP ≥130/85, FPG ≥100. Children: TC <170 / 170–199 / ≥200; LDL-C <110 / 110–129 / ≥130.
explanation.differs: US vs Endocrine Society vs ESC triglyceride bands; LDL-C ≥190 (no calculator) vs 70–189 (risk-based); high vs moderate vs low intensity; consensus metabolic syndrome (TG ≥150) vs 2018 AHA/ACC risk-enhancer tally (TG >175); adult vs pediatric cut-points.
explanation.examAngle: Expect: count metabolic syndrome criteria from a case, pick the statin plan for LDL-C ≥190, identify a high-intensity statin dose, classify a child’s LDL-C, or state why triglycerides ≥500 mg/dL are treated.

comparisons.distinguisher: Pediatric cut-points come from population percentiles and are much lower.

takeaway: An LDL cholesterol of 190 mg/dL or more calls for a high-intensity statin without a risk calculation, severe hypertriglyceridemia starts at 500 mg/dL in the 2018 American guideline, metabolic syndrome needs three of five criteria, and children are already high at a total cholesterol of 200 or an LDL cholesterol of 130 mg/dL.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old without known cardiovascular disease has an LDL-C of 210 mg/dL. Under the 2018 AHA/ACC cholesterol guideline, what is the recommended approach?

options.text: Begin high-intensity statin therapy without calculating 10-year ASCVD risk
options.rationale: Correct. LDL-C ≥190 mg/dL is severe primary hypercholesterolaemia; risk calculation is not needed.

options.text: Calculate 10-year ASCVD risk and treat only if it is ≥7.5%
options.rationale: Incorrect. The risk-based pathway applies to adults 40–75 with LDL-C 70–189 mg/dL.
Incorrect. High-intensity therapy (≥50% LDL-C lowering) is recommended at LDL-C ≥190 mg/dL.
Incorrect. The guideline’s LDL-C ≥190 take-home message sets no age-40 threshold and needs no risk score; the 40–75 age band belongs to the risk-based pathway.

questions.stem: Which regimen is classified as high-intensity statin therapy (expected LDL-C reduction ≥50%) in the 2018 AHA/ACC guideline?

options.rationale: Correct. Rosuvastatin 20–40 mg and atorvastatin 40–80 mg are high intensity.
Incorrect. Atorvastatin 10–20 mg is moderate intensity (30–49%).
Incorrect. Simvastatin 20–40 mg is moderate intensity.
Incorrect. Pravastatin 10–20 mg is low intensity (<30%).

questions.stem: A 14-year-old has an LDL-C of 135 mg/dL. Using the NHLBI 2011 pediatric cut-points, how is this classified?

options.rationale: Correct. Pediatric LDL-C ≥130 mg/dL is high.
Incorrect. The pediatric acceptable LDL-C is <110 mg/dL.
Incorrect. 135 mg/dL is above the borderline-high range.

options.text: Cannot be classified because children use adult cut-points
options.rationale: Incorrect. Children have their own percentile-based table.

claims.text: Triglyceride classifications differ by guideline; severe HTG treated to prevent pancreatitis with fibrates/omega-3, goal <500.
LDL-C ≥190 → high-intensity statin without risk calculation; ezetimibe if ≥100; adult FH suspicion >190.
Statin intensity definitions and doses; primary-prevention ≥7.5% pathway.
Metabolic syndrome any 3 of 5 with population-specific waist; 2018 AHA/ACC tally uses TG >175.
NHLBI 2011 pediatric TC and LDL-C cut-points.
Reviewer’s four-band triglyceride scheme (<150/150–199/200–499/≥500) and FH suspicion at LDL-C ≥160 under age 20.
claims.note: Not taught as facts: no open source read in this session states the four-band scheme; Nordestgaard 2016 flags children at >155 mg/dL.

accuracyFlags.issue: Ch. 18 Hit 3 gives one set of triglyceride bands (<150 normal, 150–199 borderline high, 200–499 high, ≥500 very high). Hernandez 2021 tabulates three current schemes, none identical: 2018 AHA/ACC normal <175, moderate 175–499, severe ≥500; Endocrine Society mild 150–199, moderate 200–999, severe ≥1000; ESC severe >880. US/European guidelines; Philippine guidelines not covered (register flag rv-tg-categories-scheme).

Ch. 18 Hit 8 lists waist ≥102/88 cm and TG ≥150. Kassi 2011: the consensus definition uses population-specific waist cut-offs (IDF 90/80 cm for South and South-East Asian, Chinese and Japanese people); the 2018 AHA/ACC risk-enhancer table tallies TG >175 mg/dL. Philippine guidelines not covered (register flag rv-mets-cutoffs-guideline).
